title: ≤0.100.x clients can never detect v0.101.x — 4-part release tag unparseable by old VersionHelper (silent "up to date")

status.label: Legacy-client update reachability plan needed
status.detail: The incompatibility is substantiated; release-side bridge versus manual-upgrade mitigation needs validation.

judgment.rationale: The reporter’s latest update demonstrates that the reported 0.100.2 client detected and installed v0.102.3001 after that release used a three-part tag. This resolves the current reachability failure for the reporter; preserve the future tag-format regression risk, but do not propose a separate code fix or release action for an issue already mitigated by the published release.
evidence: The issue author reports running 0.100.2 Stable and says the current v0.102.3001 release uses a three-part tag.
The same author reports that 0.100.2 detected and upgraded to v0.102.3001 successfully.
The original issue includes a diagnostic summary confirming an update check ran and returned up-to-date for the earlier four-part tag.
PR #49414 introduced four-part version support after the 0.100.2 client shipped.

The newest reply links PR51582 as the release-tag correction. The reporter already confirmed successful detection and upgrade through the three-part v0.102.3001 tag; a commenter claiming a backport is not independent release verification.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat the reported failure as mitigated by the three-part v0.102.3001 release tag; avoid a competing fix proposal and retain the tag-format risk as context.

fix_assessment.rationale: The release’s three-part v0.102.3001 tag supplies a public, reporter-verified bridge for the observed old-client update failure. The issue remains open, and no claim is made that future four-part tags would be compatible.

issue_context.summary: The reported old-client update failure is mitigated by the three-part v0.102.3001 tag; future four-part tags remain a regression risk.
